resolutions.researcher_notes: Read both wiki-harvested seed citations. archive.aawsat.com (4 May 2002, Asharq Al-Awsat) confirms the project itself was real and well-advanced: Egypt/Libya's jointly-owned Arab pipeline company (ATUBE, 50/50 EGPC/Libya NOC) had 'completed technical studies for the crude oil pipeline project from Tobruk to Alexandria,' 620 km (495 km Egypt / 125 km Libya), 150,000 b/d capacity -- but this article describes the PLANNING phase, not a cancellation, and predates the sheet's 2004/2006 dates. thefreelibrary.com's 'Libya-Chad Oil Pipeline To Cameroon' article (403, bot-walled) is about a wholly different route/corridor and would not support this unit even if read. No source found stating the pipeline was cancelled specifically in 2006 or shelved in 2004. Notably, GEM's own wiki page for this pipeline attributes 'presumed to be cancelled as of 2006 due to lack of evidence for further development' to this SAME 2002 aawsat article -- i.e. that appears to be GEM's own dormancy inference (no further news found past a certain point), not a documented cancellation date in the cited source itself. Consistent with that reading, ShelvedCancelledType should likely be 'inferred' rather than sourced to a real cancellation announcement, but that is a recommendation for Update, not a citation.
No source found giving 2004 as a shelving date -- see Status [ref] notes. The one substantive seed citation (aawsat 2002) describes active planning, not a shelving event.

No source found giving 2006 as a cancellation date -- see Status [ref] notes for the full analysis, including that GEM's own wiki entry appears to have derived '2006' as a presumed-dormancy cutoff from the same 2002 planning-stage article, not from a documented cancellation announcement.
